observed_original_abi.receiver: ECX carries the receiver, and the record says so at R1-VFT (INFERRED) with conventions.confidence SUPPORTED / corroboration persisted_agrees. The record's own words: 0x00a85840 is slot 6 of the vptr-backed vftable at 0x01458024, the body reads its incoming ECX before writing it, and incoming_ecx_reads is 1. In the listing that read is 0x00a85867 `MOV ESI,ECX` (obs-0013 REG_READ, obs-0014 REG_WRITE), and the ECX value is used as a base 0x00a858a7 `LEA ECX,[ESI + 0x24]`, whose result is handed to 0x00537dc0 as that callee's hidden receiver. So the record's bounds_only true / offsets [] / distinct_offsets 0 / written_through 0 is its own statement that it saw no load and no store through the receiver -- which agrees with the listing, where the ONLY receiver-relative operand in the thirty-one instructions is that LEA, which forms an address and touches nothing. The alias-aware scan in tools/reconstruction_tooling/evidence_fields.receiver_offsets over this listing with register ECX attributes exactly one displacement to the receiver, 0x24, read through register ESI, must=True, unresolved=[] bounded=True; 0x24 is a DISPLACEMENT and no field name or layout is attached to it in either direction.

observed_original_abi.record_incompleteness: abi_derived.stack_arguments enumerates ONE slot (entry_ESP+0x8, ordinal 2, observed, read false, sizes [4]) with gaps 1 and total_bytes 8, and its abstained_because reads "flow_not_modelled: the linear ESP walk ends at +12, so the listing is not one path". That abstention is about a LINEAR ESP walk, which cannot see what a callee does to ESP across a CALL. The two facts it missed are the three callee-popped PUSHes (0x00a8587f, 0x00a85898, 0x00a858a6, each consumed by that callee's own RET 0x4) and the second [ESP+0x40] read, which is why the body has TWO caller arguments and why the two reads are of different arguments. The machine record is not edited; the reading is stated here and in the staging header, with its own evidence (the three callees' terminators, read out of the same image).
observed_original_abi.return_observation: return_type is void, and that is a SOURCE-SIDE choice with the machine evidence stated, not a recovered fact. (1) The machine record's own return sub-record names XMM0 with register_class float_or_x87 at confidence APPROXIMATION, and its stated basis is inference RT1: "an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body". That is a property of every SSE instruction ever written, not of a return. (2) The last XMM0 write in the listing is 0x00a85889 `MOVSS [ESP + 0x18],XMM0`, a STORE to the frame, 0x2a bytes before the terminator at 0x00a858b3, and no instruction after it writes XMM0. (3) The last EAX write is 0x00a85894 `MOV EAX,[ESP + 0x40]`, whose only consumer is the PUSH at 0x00a85898, and two calls run after that, so the EAX the caller receives is whatever 0x00537dc0 left. Reading 0x00537dc0's own 80-instruction listing settles what that is: its last instruction before the epilogue on BOTH arms is 0x00537e8c `MOV EAX,[EBP + -0x4]`, i.e. its own hidden receiver, which is the address this body built at 0x00a858a7 -- receiver + 0x24. (4) This body contains no instruction that places a value in a return register at the terminator, so a C++ `return f(...)` and a C++ void body are byte-identical here and the machine cannot tell them apart. void is the weaker of the two readings and is the one taken. The model test pins the mechanics either way: case F drives a sentinel through the last callee and requires it handed straight back, and case M compares the entry against a cdecl twin through one harness.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics_disagreement: UNRESOLVED AND DELIBERATELY NOT ARBITRATED. The ABI envelope names return_register XMM0 and return_semantics float_or_x87_in_XMM0; this package declares void. The record is not corrected and the disagreement is left standing: the record's stated basis (RT1) is a linear-walk artefact of the same kind as the stack-argument abstention, but nothing in these 118 bytes can settle it, and this body has no incoming call edge (it is vtable slot 6) so there is no caller whose use of EAX or XMM0 could be read. Settling it needs a run of the original that records what the caller reads.

implementation.declaration: extern "C" void PKG_W2_00A85840_NAKED_THISCALL re_00a85840(Receiver*, Word*, Word*);
implementation.linkage: C language linkage, on a __thiscall member. The convention token is carried by the package macro PKG_W2_00A85840_NAKED_THISCALL, which the staging header defines as __attribute__((naked, thiscall)) on GCC/Clang and __declspec(naked) __thiscall on MSVC, so the token `thiscall` is reachable from the target source span -- which is what the validator's convention resolution follows.
implementation.shape: A NAKED, BYTE-FAITHFUL TRANSCRIPTION of the target's own 118 bytes, not a C++ restatement, and the choice is deliberate. The body stores six words of argument 2 into the frame at THREE different stack-pointer values, in the listing's own order, because the loads were issued in that order and the spills follow the live ranges. A C++ restatement would have to choose an order for the two overlapping bytes at S+0x00..S+0x03, and choosing one is a claim the listing does not make in that form. Emitting the listing's own order and its own three stack-pointer values preserves it by construction. The convention claim and the bytes claim are two separate claims, and a transcription makes both: __thiscall is the machine's determination (R1-VFT + C6B) and the 118 bytes are read back out of the image and pinned by the model test.
implementation.argument_surface: The parameters are left unnamed on purpose: the function is naked, so it has no C++ body to read them in, and a named parameter in a naked definition is an unused-parameter diagnostic under -Wextra on every compiler. The declared types describe the shape the machine enters this with -- a receiver pointer in ECX, and one 32-bit word at each of entry_ESP+0x4 and entry_ESP+0x8 -- and the model test drives it through a call site that builds exactly that shape. NEITHER WORD IS NAMED FOR WHAT IT IS. Argument 1 is read at 0x00a85894, pushed at 0x00a85898 and handed to 0x00537f40 without being dereferenced anywhere in these 118 bytes, so the model test drives it over eight values including unmapped ones, which is only sound BECAUSE the body never looks. Argument 2 is dereferenced at six displacements.
implementation.callee_declarations: The three direct callees are declared in the staging header with their addresses in their names, which is the convention the validator reads to compare the source's call set against the xref export, and are DEFINED as observers in the model test. No C++ class member is named for any of them and the hidden receiver's declared type is the same opaque Receiver this body takes.

observed_mechanics: 0x00a85840 SUB ESP,0x38 -- the only frame instruction (abi_derived.parse.frame: push_ebp false, mov_ebp_esp false, sub 56, local_extent 0). With S = entry_ESP - 0x38, it is what makes 0x00a85843's [ESP + 0x40] land on entry_ESP + 0x8.

0x00a85843 MOV EAX,[ESP+0x40] -- EAX = the word at entry_ESP+0x8, the SECOND ordinary stack argument, and the only pointer this body dereferences. It is read through at six displacements by 0x00a85847, 0x00a8584c, 0x00a85856, 0x00a85861, 0x00a85869 and 0x00a85872.

0x00a85847..0x00a85889 -- six copies out of argument 2 into the frame, at the SAME displacement each is read from: 0x04 and 0x08 as four-byte SSE moves, 0x0c and 0x10 as four-byte SSE moves, 0x00 and 0x02 as 16-bit moves. The displacement of the store is not the displacement of the MOVSS operand text: the stack pointer is entry-0x38, entry-0x3c and entry-0x40 at the three different points the stores run, which is why the frame offsets are +0x04, +0x08, +0x10, +0x18, +0x00, +0x00 and +0x02 rather than the source offsets.

0x00a85866 PUSH ESI / 0x00a858af POP ESI -- the only register this body saves, and a save/restore pair that brackets all three calls (abi_derived.saved_registers ["ESI"], obs-0012 REG_READ, obs-0027 REG_RESTORE). Nothing between them writes ESI.

0x00a85867 MOV ESI,ECX -- the receiver is aliased, unadjusted, and never re-read from ECX. Two calls run between this and the LEA, so a callee that rewrote ECX would change what 0x00a858a7 reaches; the alias is what makes the body insensitive to that. This is also the alias the FIELDS/OFFSETS alias-aware scan follows, and the reason the record's own receiver enumeration (offsets []) is empty while the listing does reach a receiver displacement.

0x00a85877 ADD EAX,0x14 / 0x00a8587f PUSH EAX -- the base handed to 0x0041cb40 is argument 2 + 0x14, so the window is argument 2 + 0x14 .. + 0x37 and the two arguments are the same offset into two objects that share a layout.

0x00a85880 LEA ECX,[ESP+0x1c] with ESP at entry-0x40, i.e. entry-0x24 -- the first call's hidden receiver is S+0x14, the SAME object's +0x14 member and not a second variable. 0x0041cb40's own 64-instruction body copies nine dwords (0x24 bytes) from its word to offsets 0x00..0x20 of its receiver, and S+0x14 + 0x24 = S+0x38, the top of the reservation: the window is exactly this body's frame.

0x00a85894 MOV EAX,[ESP+0x40] with ESP at entry-0x3c -- the SECOND read of the same displacement, and it names entry_ESP+0x4, a DIFFERENT caller argument. The two ESP values differ because all three callees pop their own single word with RET 0x4. This is the fact a linear ESP walk cannot see and the one its abstained_because names.

0x00a85899 LEA ECX,[ESP+0x8] with ESP at entry-0x40, i.e. entry-0x38 -- the second call's hidden receiver is the WHOLE local, not its +0x14 member, so both the 0x14 bytes this body copied and the 0x24 bytes 0x0041cb40 wrote are in scope for it. Its word is argument 1.

0x00a858a2 LEA ECX,[ESP+0x4] with ESP at entry-0x3c, i.e. entry-0x38, then 0x00a858a6 PUSH ECX -- the third call's word is the address of the whole local, the same address the second call was handed as its receiver.

0x00a858a7 LEA ECX,[ESI+0x24] -- the ONLY thing this body ever does with the receiver: it forms the address of receiver+0x24 and hands it to 0x00537dc0 as that callee's hidden receiver. No byte is read and none is written through the receiver, in any register, anywhere in these 118 bytes, which is what the machine receiver record states (bounds_only true, offsets [], written_through 0) and what this package does not turn into a field or a layout.

0x00a858aa CALL 0x00537dc0 -- the callee's EAX is what reaches the caller, because POP ESI, ADD ESP and RET write no general-purpose register. Reading 0x00537dc0's own listing: its last instruction before the epilogue on both the overwrite arm and the skip arm is 0x00537e8c `MOV EAX,[EBP + -0x4]`, so it hands back its own hidden receiver, which is the address this body built at 0x00a858a7.

0x00a858b0 ADD ESP,0x38 / 0x00a858b3 RET 0x8 -- the frame balances to exactly the entry stack pointer and the terminator then drops the two callee-popped words, so the caller resumes at entry_ESP+0x8. The balance is only possible if all three pushes were consumed, which is what the three callees' RET 0x4 terminators, read out of the same image, settle independently.

CONTROL FLOW: one basic block. Thirty-one instructions, zero conditional branches, zero loops, zero second exits, so all three calls happen on every execution in the order the addresses give. Nothing in the body branches on the receiver or on either argument, and the model test has cases that kill a null-check, an early return on a null receiver and a branch on the frame.

GLOBALS: none. The 31 instructions name no data-segment address; the immediates that are addresses are 0x0041cb40, 0x00537f40 and 0x00537dc0, all inside .text. The record's globals category is empty and the xref export carries no data-reference edge type for this VA.

VIRTUAL DISPATCH: none in the body, and none declared. abi_derived.dispatch records indirect_calls 0, call_offsets [] and vtable_shaped_loads 0, and the 31 instructions contain no register- or memory-operand transfer. The body is itself a slot occupant, which is the opposite of dispatching: it never reads the word at the receiver's +0x00, and the receiver's only use is to form an interior address for a callee to take as ITS receiver. So no slot boundary is declared and no dispatch pointer is modelled as a member.

VTABLE SLOT: GhidraMCP /read_memory at 0x01458018 for 48 bytes puts, from 0x01458024: 0x00a85070, 0x004ae250, 0x00a850d0, 0x00a85790, 0x007edc60, 0x00a858c0 and 0x00a85840 at 0x0145803c -- the seventh dword, slot index 6, and the single incoming code reference ghidra_function.xrefs records for this VA. GhidraMCP /read_memory at 0x01458018 len 48 returns 00000034 ffffffff 0000404b 7050a800 50e24a00 d050a800 9057a800 60dc7e00 c058a800 4058a800 30129500 40e65200, and a direct PE read of the same 48 bytes at RVA 0x1148018 returns the identical sequence. vtables.not_claimed: no class, no vtable identity, no receiver type, no object size, no vtable-pointer offset, no field and no slot boundary. The table is a run of .text words and a slot is not a class; this binary carries no MSVC RTTI and no SDK name is recorded for it.

types_note: Receiver is declared and deliberately left UNDEFINED (`struct Receiver;`). The record determines that the receiver arrives in ECX and that the body forms exactly one address from it, receiver+0x24; it determines nothing about what the receiver IS. An empty definition would be a claim that there are no members rather than a statement that none was observed, and the 0x24 is an immediate out of one instruction, not a field. No struct is named for the frame, for argument 2 or for the 0x38-byte object any of the three callees may hold, and no member is named anywhere in this package.
semantic_findings: The body's two stack arguments are read at TWO DIFFERENT ESP values, and that is the whole reason the machine ABI record under-reports them. 0x00a85843 reads entry+8 (ESP = entry-0x38) and 0x00a85894 reads entry+4 (ESP = entry-0x3c, because all three callees clean their own single stack argument with RET 0x4). The envelope's abstained_because names the cause as a linear ESP walk that ends at +12.

There is ONE local object, not two, and the overlap is the least obvious fact in the body: 0x00a85880's LEA resolves to S+0x14, which is inside the same 0x38-byte object 0x00a85899 hands to 0x00537f40 and 0x00a858a6 hands to 0x00537dc0.

The first call's destination and its source are the same offset into two objects: the pushed pointer is argument 2 + 0x14 and the hidden receiver is the local's +0x14, so 0x0041cb40 copies 0x24 bytes from argument 2 + 0x14 to the local + 0x14. The window S+0x14 .. S+0x37 is exactly the tail of this body's frame.
Argument 1 is read, pushed and handed on and is never dereferenced anywhere in these 118 bytes. Nothing constrains what it is, so the model test drives it over eight values including unmapped ones.

The 0x38-byte local's first 0x14 bytes are a byte-for-byte copy of argument 2's first twenty bytes, reassembled from two 16-bit loads and four 32-bit loads. The ORDER in which the two overlapping bytes at S+0x00..S+0x03 are written is a machine fact and the reconstruction preserves it by emitting the listing's order rather than by restating it as a copy.

The third callee's conditional arms decide whether receiver+0x24 is overwritten or kept, so whether the merge actually lands depends on 0x00537dc0 and on the two callees before it. This body is indifferent -- it passes and returns -- so nothing in these 118 bytes can answer it, and the package does not claim an answer.

The receiver is never loaded or stored through. The ONLY receiver-relative operand in the whole body is the LEA at 0x00a858a7, and a LEA forms an address and touches nothing. So the record's offsets [] and written_through 0 are statements about the body, not about the record's blindness, and the alias-aware scan's single proven displacement 0x24 is an address computation rather than a field access.

unresolved_questions: THE DECLARED RETURN TYPE IS A SOURCE-SIDE CHOICE THE MACHINE CANNOT SETTLE. The machine return state is UNCLASSIFIED: the ABI record names XMM0, and evidence_returns.classify returns UNCLASSIFIED on that alone -- "the machine fixes where the value travels and not the C type, and no width can be claimed". There is no width record, no return_semantics string that is a C type, and no incoming call edge to read a caller's use of EAX or XMM0. void and T* are byte-identical here because the body contains no instruction that places a value in a return register at the terminator. void was taken as the weaker claim. The disagreement with the record's XMM0 is recorded, not arbitrated.

WHAT 0x00537dc0's FOUR CONDITIONAL ARMS DECIDE. 0x00537dd7, 0x00537df4, 0x00537e09 and 0x00537e31 choose whether receiver+0x24 is overwritten or kept, so whether the merge lands is decided by that callee and by the two before it. This body is indifferent: it passes and returns. The two helpers it calls internally, 0x0041dd30 and 0x0041dd90, are not modelled either.

WHAT 0x00537f40 DOES beyond being called. Its own body was not read for this package; only its terminator (0x00537ff5 RET 0x4) was. So the +0x04..+0x0c region of the local and the 0x24 bytes the second callee writes at its receiver's +0x14 are uncharacterised, and the local's 0x38 extent is a requirement of that callee's own listing rather than a claim about the helpers.

THE 0x6c OBJECT SIZE AND EVERY RECEIVER MEMBER ABOVE +0x24. The +0x24 LEA and 0x00537dc0's own extent bound this body at 0x5c on its own. The 0x6c figure in this package's earlier revision came from 0x00a853b0, a DIFFERENT listing, and it is not used here.

THE DOMAIN TYPES. ghidra_function.sdk_name is null for this VA, there is no MSVC RTTI in this binary, and the four listings read here fix offsets and widths but no names. Every member in this package is an immediate out of an instruction and nothing is named for a field.

THE PROVENANCE OF BOTH STACK WORDS. Both are plain pointers the body only reads or only forwards, and neither has a call site to inspect, so the argument order and types of every caller are outside this evidence. The arity of two comes from the terminator alone.

NO DECOMPILATION EXISTS for this VA in this session: the evidence pack's decompilation category is absent and there is no second, independently-derived reading to cross-check the reconstruction against.

WHETHER THE FOUR BYTES AT ARGUMENT 2 + 0x14 ARE ONE OBJECT OR A POINTER. 0x0041cb40 copies them as three of its nine dwords; the bytes move verbatim either way, so the two readings are byte-identical in this package and what the value means is outside this body.

HOW FAR THE TABLE AT 0x01458024 RUNS. Seven words from 0x01458024 to 0x0145803f are transcribed, and the run of .text-looking words continues past the own slot (0x00951230, 0x0052e640 at 0x01458040..0x01458047). notes: No validation check was weakened, disabled or special-cased. src/ is integrator-owned and was not touched. The earlier revision's intended_paths named src/editor/pkg_w2_00a85840_types.hpp, a file that does not exist; source_files and intended_paths now name only the three real staging files.

The two blockers this revision was opened for are both closed, and both by making the source agree with the machine rather than by restating the record. FIELDS/OFFSETS reached PASS/complete because the reconstruction is now a naked transcription that declares no field offset or member name, so the check's own alias-aware scan is the witness and it attributes exactly one receiver displacement, 0x24, read through the ESI alias at 0x00a858a7. RETURN SEMANTICS reached PASS because the sidecar now carries the machine record's own return fields (return_register XMM0, return_semantics float_or_x87_in_XMM0) alongside a declared return_type of void, and the source declares void; the machine return state is UNCLASSIFIED and stays that way, and the disagreement is recorded in return_semantics_disagreement rather than resolved.

The near-twin 0x00a98400 is the same thirty-one instructions with exactly one displacement different, 0x18 against 0x24. Its package was read before this one was written and used as a structural reference; every target-specific value -- the 118 bytes, the three rel32 displacements, the table base 0x01458024 and its seven words, the receiver register reads, the conventions confidence, which is SUPPORTED here and was INFERRED there -- was re-derived from the image and from this target's own evidence pack.
